analysis: Examined four changes: (1) docs/architecture/inference.md adds a paragraph (head lines 2336-2347) about Flint constrained-decode chaining and automatic paged selection; documentation only. (2) provider-swift/.../EngineV2KVBackendPolicy.swift adds the exact ID "RecursiveSI/flint-int4" to the auto-paged allowlist (head lines 37-41). This is exact-string matching, with no substring or alias. Per-model config, the kill switch DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PAGED_KV, the VLM span-mask veto and the crash-loop guard in the same file are untouched. Flint is already described as paged-only, so auto selection matches the intended backend. It does not change auth, attestation, encryption or the coordinator wire contract. (3) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule pointer moves from f77b384 to fbd2cd0. Only the pointer is visible, with no submodule diff. The docs describe constrained chaining in the SDK engine (step N+1 sampled speculatively using the previous state's mask, then redrawn from retained logits when state diverges). That could in principle affect output-constraint correctness, RNG/penalty state restoration, or per-request state isolation (T-007, T-041 cache scope). It is not verifiable from the supplied evidence. This is an unverified contract, not a finding. Cache-related threat T-041 is unchanged here. The paged-default change for Flint affects KV backend selection and SSD prefix-cache eligibility only through existing gates (per-donation, TTL, HMAC lookup, cacheSalt scoping), which this PR does not alter. Remaining questions for deeper review: submodule contents (constrained chaining, mask cache keyed by state only, confirming no cross-request mask or state leakage and that the FlintAnswerStops/constraint behavior is fail-closed), and whether paged serving of Flint via the SSD tier preserves salt scoping.
